rationale: Evidence from iteration 1 (score 225.15, up from 26.05): no trial failed on controller exceptions or stalls. Every run ended by off_track except 3 oval finishes. Max error sits at 0.060 to 0.067 m, just past the 0.06 m off-track limit, and line_loss_events is 0.25 to 1 per trial, so the robot drifts out at bends rather than oscillating. Steering oscillation stayed low (0.23 to 0.35), so the damping is not the main problem. Oval finishes in about 1.68 s, so speed headroom exists when the line is held. Off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which tops out near 0.0575 even at body_width 0.18, so the limit cannot be widened and the fix must come from tracking. Changes: (1) kp 4.0 to 5.0 for stronger correction at bends; (2) kd 0.3 to 0.6 to damp the larger correction; (3) base_speed 1.3 to 1.1 to give steering more time per bend, since the oval finish time leaves room, though I expect completion_time to rise to about 2.0 to 2.4 s; (4) sensor_size 0.012 to 0.016 so the sum of readings stays above the 0.05 line-loss threshold further from the line; (5) sensors spread to x = +/-0.07 with 0.035 spacing and y = 0.07 to see the line earlier and catch drift sooner; (6) wheel_track 0.10 to 0.09 for more turn rate per PWM count; (7) mass 0.6 to 0.5 kg to cut yaw inertia. body_length, body_width, wheel_radius and sensor weights are unchanged. Expected result: line_loss_events below 0.5, max_error below 0.05, more oval finishes and s-bend progress above 0.8. Hypotheses to test: H1, kp 5 with the wider sensor array reduces max_error; H2, the larger sensor size removes most line-loss events; H3, lower base_speed trades some time for completion. Next measurements: progress and completion (did the bend drift stop), completion_time (cost of slower speed), max_error and line_loss_events (where the line is still lost), and steering_oscillation (whether kp 5 with kd 0.6 is too stiff).
